q: How does a Firozabad glass unit count CO2 from soda ash and limestone in the batch?
title: Firozabad glass: process CO2 from batch
short: Carbonates in the batch release CO2 when they melt: about 0.415 t per tonne of soda ash, 0.440 t per tonne of limestone and 0.477 t per tonne of dolomite, by IPCC 2006. This process CO2 is Scope 1, added to the furnace gas.
audience: Glass and bangle units in the Firozabad cluster of Uttar Pradesh

p: Tonnes of each carbonate from purchase or stock records.
Add to Scope 1 alongside gas burned in the furnace.
Recycled glass (cullet) has no carbonates left to release, so more cullet means less process CO2 per tonne melted.

example.title: Worked example: one month (illustrative quantities)
lines: Soda ash: 1,000 kg x 0.415 = 415 kg CO2
example.note: Quantities are illustrative; factors are IPCC 2006 stoichiometric values for full calcination.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.

sources.label: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
